correctness.rationale: An exact coupling reduces each completed target class to a quota of opposite source selections, giving the stated binomial-strip CDF and positive-part binomial mean for every finite a,b,q. Independent rational Markov-chain enumeration agrees on 1470 checks, including boundary sizes. Triangular binomial CLT plus uniform integrability gives the asymmetric piecewise-normal law and mean; F has strictly positive second derivative and a unique Gaussian-quantile minimizer. Endpoint divergence gives finite minimizers and quota lower bounds force the O(N^{-1/2}) window for all of them. The ratio under uniform vertices follows from a binomial L1 law of large numbers. This does not assume experiments prove asymptotics.

originality.rationale: The claim is a new asymptotic optimal *independently reweighted source sampling* theorem, not a reformulation of prior uniform-source covering bounds or Markov-walk cover times. Deng–Wang give the basic process and fixed-degree complete-bipartite tail, including a related two-clique quota lower bound, but not q-dependent exact completion laws or minimization. Dimitrov–Plaxton treat uniform source sampling and neighbor selection. Published published-finding corpus matches concern random walks with path-constrained sources. Residual risk is generic unindexed two-quota optimal-sampling theory, not affirmative coverage.
residual_risks: Generic or unindexed two-quota optimal-sampling/negative-binomial scheduling results might imply the Gaussian-quantile correction without using graph language.
Relevant public published-finding corpus random-walk records were checked by title/summary only, not through full repository bodies; they describe distinct sampling dynamics.
Independent expert assessment of originality has not been performed.

value.rationale: Alon-type graph coverage is a natural setting to ask whether changing source-vertex sampling can overcome slow completion. On K_{a,b}, uniform vertex selection has a linear waiting penalty at unequal fixed class proportions, while optimally fixed iid class choices attain the information-theoretic first-order lower bound N with only square-root excess. The unique nonzero Gaussian-quantile correction improves upon naïve reverse-proportion matching at the same square-root order; the complete limit law quantifies fluctuations. This is a structurally motivated optimal-design boundary, not an arbitrary finite table or a mere variance computation.
